surprises.description: AVBH reported diluted EPS of $0.94, above the preview’s $0.868 consensus estimate and its $0.80–$0.87 base-case range. Net income was $10.2 million versus the preview’s implied estimate of about $9.4 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net income rose to $10.2 million ($0.94 per diluted share) in Q3 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS (diluted) | Q3'26 Consensus | $0.868”; “My base case: revenue ~$28.9M, EPS ~$0.83”; base scenario EPS “$0.80–0.87.”

surprises.description: Reported NIM fell to 4.07%, below the preview’s 4.20% management-guide reference and its 4.20%–4.26% base-case range. The preview specifically treated 4.15% or lower as a warning level; management attributed most of the decline to unusually high cash balances.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net interest margin fell 19 basis points to 4.07%, with 17 basis points attributed to $205 million higher average cash balances; management estimates a normalized margin closer to the low 4.20s.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management guided NIM down toward 4.20%”; base scenario: “NIM 4.20–4.26%”; “≤4.15% = funding costs are winning.”

surprises.description: A temporary $270 million client deposit is expected to leave in Q4, creating a sizable near-term deposit outflow that the preview did not identify. Core deposits grew about $76 million excluding that temporary balance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Core deposit growth was approximately $76 million excluding brokered deposits and a temporary $270 million client deposit that management expects to leave in Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview discussed deposit growth and funding mix but did not mention a temporary $270 million deposit or its expected Q4 departure.

surprises.description: AVBH reported a modest rise in nonperforming loans after placing a $1.5 million land loan on nonaccrual, rather than reporting the deterioration risks highlighted in the preview around the $29 million CRE relationship and criticized SaaS loans. The increase is limited, with essentially no net charge-offs and no broad-based credit deterioration.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Nonperforming loans rose modestly to 70 basis points of total loans after a $1.5 million land loan was placed on nonaccrual, while net charge-offs were essentially zero with no broad-based credit deterioration.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “the $29M non-owner-occupied CRE relationship” and “two criticized horizontal-SaaS loans, ~$4M,” and said a new non-accrual or further criticized-loan increases were key risks.

surprises.description: Instead of a possible first buyback, AVBH issued $30 million of new subordinated debt and redeemed its existing $22 million issuance. The refinancing and added debt were not anticipated in the preview, which described the bank as overcapitalized and identified a buyback as a possible surprise.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company issued $30 million of new subordinated debt and redeemed its existing $22 million issuance to support organic growth while maintaining capital ratios.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Overcapitalized post-IPO with no dividend. At ~1.15x book, a first buyback authorization would be a genuine surprise.”

surprises.description: Management said Q4 expenses should be flat to slightly higher, a milder outlook than the preview’s expectation that expenses would step up with hiring and the SBA investment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Noninterest expense fell to $15.1 million from $16.5 million (which included a $2.6 million litigation settlement), with management guiding Q4 expenses flat to slightly up.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario expected “expenses step up on SBA/hiring”; the preview also said new hires and the SBA division “lift the run rate.”

surprises.description: Management put a specific through-the-cycle deposit-beta target on the record—below 50%, ideally closer to 40%—which the preview had not anticipated. A lower beta target would imply less deposit-cost pass-through over a rate cycle.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company [is] targeting a through-the-cycle deposit beta below 50%, ideally closer to 40%.”
